questions.question: When making a regular stop on a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Use only the front brake.
Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
Use only the rear brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the front and rear brakes at the same time.
questions.explanation: For a regular stop, use both the front and rear brakes together. Then downshift as you slow down.

questions.question: Your lane position should:

options.text: Help you blend in with traffic.
Give you a way to escape if danger appears.
Encourage other drivers to share your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a way to escape if danger appears.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see others and be seen. It keeps you away from wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It also discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if a problem occurs.

questions.question: What should a motorcycle rider do to avoid collisions?

options.text: Keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
Ride slowly at all times.
Ride in the center of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance from other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Keep plenty of space around your motorcycle. Maintain this space when following others, being followed, passing, being passed, or sharing a lane.

questions.question: Why should you flash your brake light?

options.text: To tell other drivers you are riding near them.
To help other drivers see you in slow traffic.
To warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: To warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Flash your brake light when you slow down in places where other drivers might not expect it. This is especially important before making sharp, fast turns off highways.

questions.question: When should you wear reflective clothing?

options.text: Only at night.
Only during the day.
Both day and night.

questions.correctAnswerText: Both day and night.
questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen during the day. Wear bright, reflective clothing every time you ride, whether it is day or night.

questions.question: When slowing or stopping your motorcycle, what should you do with the gears?

options.text: Do not change gears.
Shift up through the gears.
Shift down through the gears.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift down through the gears.
questions.explanation: Shift down through the gears as you slow or stop. When stopped, stay in first gear so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: The Motorcycle Safety Foundation teaches a SEE strategy for safe riding. What does SEE mean?

options.text: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
Slow, Experienced, and Error-free.
Safe, Experienced, and Evasive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Search, Evaluate, and Execute.
questions.explanation: SEE stands for Search, Evaluate, and Execute. Good riders use this strategy to make safe decisions while riding.

questions.question: When the lights are flashing at a railroad crossing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go slowly and be careful.
Turn around and find another route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: Stop completely when lights flash at a railroad crossing. Wait until the train passes and the lights stop flashing before you go. Never try to outrun a train.

questions.question: When should you use the engine cut-off switch and pull the clutch?

options.text: When the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it.
When you start losing control in a turn.
When the motorcycle starts to shake or wobble.

questions.correctAnswerText: When the throttle gets stuck and you cannot free it.
questions.explanation: If the throttle gets stuck, immediately turn off the engine and pull the clutch. This cuts power to the rear wheel so you can safely slow down and stop.

questions.question: How should your jacket and pants fit when riding?

options.text: Loose enough for wind to catch the fabric.
Snug enough to prevent flapping in the wind.
So tight you cannot move freely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Snug enough to prevent flapping in the wind.
questions.explanation: Your jacket and pants should fit snugly so they do not flap in the wind. They should also be loose enough that you can move and stretch.

questions.question: When you reach an uncontrolled intersection at the same time as another vehicle, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
Flash your headlights to signal the other vehicle to go.
Continue through and expect the other vehicle to stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At an uncontrolled intersection with no signs or lights, the driver on the left must yield to the driver on the right.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist not rely only on mirrors?

options.text: Mirrors can get dirty and reduce visibility.
Mirrors are always unreliable.
Motorcycles have blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Motorcycles have blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any other vehicle. Mirrors alone are not enough to see everything around you.

questions.question: What is the minimum age to get a driver license in South Dakota?

options.text: 14 years old
16 years old
18 years old

questions.correctAnswerText: 14 years old
questions.explanation: In South Dakota, you must be at least 14 years old to get a driver license. You must also meet all other state requirements.

questions.question: What should a motorcyclist do when other vehicles are slowed or stopped?

options.text: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
It is okay to weave in and out of traffic lanes.
Ride in a straight line between two lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not weave between lanes of traffic.
questions.explanation: Weaving between stopped or slow vehicles is dangerous. Other vehicles may change lanes, doors may open, or arms may stick out. Motorcycles need the full width of a lane to stay safe.

questions.question: What should motorcycle passengers do?

options.text: Look over the rider's shoulder when turning or curving.
Never hold onto the rider.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look over the rider's shoulder when turning or curving.
questions.explanation: Ask your passenger to look over your shoulder in the direction of any turn or curve. This helps you and the motorcycle lean in the right direction.

questions.question: Which factor does NOT affect how fast a person's blood alcohol concentration (BAC) increases?

options.text: The number of drinks consumed
How fast a person drinks
How often a person drinks

questions.correctAnswerText: How often a person drinks
questions.explanation: Factors that affect how fast your BAC rises include the number of drinks, how fast you drink, your biological sex, your weight, and whether you have eaten recently.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves while riding over rain grooves or bridge gratings, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to cross the surface faster.
Exaggerate the zigzag motion to get other drivers' attention.
Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the grooves or gratings.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a steady speed and ride straight across the grooves or gratings.
questions.explanation: When your motorcycle weaves over grooves or gratings, maintain a steady speed and go straight across. Zigzagging to compensate is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: Which brake on a motorcycle provides the most stopping power?

options.text: The front brake
The rear brake
The emergency brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake
questions.explanation: The front brake provides about three-quarters of the motorcycle's total stopping power. Use both brakes every time you stop.

questions.question: Why should a motorcyclist change gears before starting a turn?

options.text: To prevent a sudden change in power in the middle of the turn.
To keep both hands on the handlebars during the turn.
To prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: To prevent a sudden change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you start a turn. Shifting during a turn can cause a sudden power change to the rear wheel, which may cause a skid. If you must shift during a turn, do it smoothly to avoid skidding.

questions.question: In areas with potential dangers, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Maintain their current speed.
Assume they will be safe.
Cover the clutch and both brake levers to react faster in an emergency.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and both brake levers to react faster in an emergency.
questions.explanation: In high-risk areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Cover the clutch and both brake levers so you can react quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Signal ahead
Crossroad ahead
Divided roadway ahead

questions.correctAnswerText: Divided roadway ahead
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black symbols. This sign warns you that the road ahead is divided.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Vehicles will be entering the roadway.
Signal ahead.
Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and proceed when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: Red octagonal signs are always stop signs. You must come to a complete stop, check for other traffic and pedestrians, and then proceed when it is safe.

questions.question: Lanes of traffic moving in the same direction are separated by:

options.text: White lines.
Yellow lines.
Road signs.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Solid white lines mean do not pass. Dashed white lines mean you can pass if it is safe.

questions.question: Usually a good way to handle tailgaters is to:

options.text: Get off the roadway.
Change lanes and let them pass.
Ride faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lanes and let them pass.
questions.explanation: The best way to handle tailgaters is to change lanes and let them pass. Speeding up can make the danger worse because they may continue tailgating at the higher speed.

questions.question: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should:

options.text: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
Be parked without a wheel or fender touching the curb.
Be parked parallel to the curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: Create an angle with the curb that is between 45 and 90 degrees.
questions.explanation: When parked on the road, a motorcycle should angle between 45 and 90 degrees from the curb. At least one wheel or fender should touch the curb.
